answer: Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 402 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. Because the raven height is fixed at intake and entered in the nadir receipt, the saffron audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 6 dollars per alias.
